the uterine environment is important in determining piglet survival, growth, and lactation performance.
the MUE, PigGenotype, PigletAge, and their interactions contributed to piglet growth, milk composition, lactation performance and piglet blood components during lactation.

the maternal uteroplacental environment and the impact of the uterine milieu on the development of the piglet during the prenatal period and the consequences of these effects during the postnatal period.

understanding the mechanisms by which maternal uterine and genetic effects influence piglet growth during the first 3 wk of life.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the maternal uteroplacental environment of the sow is a significant factor in preweaning survivality of piglets but not in their growth potential.
the MUE of MS sows has a detrimental effect on preweaning survivality but a positive effect on lactational performance.
both the maternal uteroplacental environment and the piglet's genotype contribute significantly to piglet growth during the lactation period.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the maternal uteroplacental environment of the MS dam may be responsible for the slower growth of piglets during the first 2 wk of lactation, but the maternal uteroplastic environment is not responsible for the slower preweaning growth of piglets from MS compared to WC dams as previously hypothesized.
the maternal uteroplacental environment is important for the development and growth of piglets during early lactation, whereas the piglet genotype is important for growth during later lactation.

the maternal uteroplacental environment is an important factor for the development of the piglet and that the maternal utero-placental environment and piglet genetics interact to affect piglet development during lactation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the maternal uteroplacental and mammary gland environment is important for piglet growth and survivability.

the maternal uteroplacental environment is a critical factor in determining the survivability and growth of the offspring during the perinatal period and throughout lactation, and this effect is dependent upon the genotype of the piglet and the maternal breed of the dam.
, in addition to the genetic contribution of the maternal dam, the uterine environment also has a significant influence on the growth and survivability of piglets.
